Funerals Under Fire

By: Sophia Phirippides | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It’s an emotional quagmire around Johannesburg’s Westpark Cemetery - gun salutes as the deceased are being laid to rest are disturbing the peace and endangering the lives of local residents.

Unique Selling Point:
Rest in peace is what we hope for when people we care about go to their final resting place. But there is no rest for the living, when ANC VIP funerals are commemorated with sprays of unrelenting gunfire, threatening the lives of innocent people who live in near the cemeteries.

When 76 year old Margaret Holloway was hit in the leg by a stray bullet in her home in Westdene, from disbanded MKMVA Kebby Maphatsoe’s funeral at Westpark Cemetery in September this year, it made headlines. National Police spokesperson Vish Naidoo, said that an investigation had been launched and people would be held accountable. When asked why the police who were present at the funeral did not act immediately, he likened the situation on ENCA to Marikana, stating that the police were preventing further bloodshed as many people were armed. ANC Deptuty Secretary Jesse Duarte called on law enforcement for a probe on what happened and condemned the firing of guns at funerals. A month later there have been no arrests.

Just this weekend at the funeral of ANC Regional Executive Committee member and former ANC Youth League Chairperson Desmond Mashele another round of bullets were fired, this time no one was injured, but many residents around Westdene and Montgomery Park, ran for cover when they heard the gunshots which lasted for over 20 minutes. They found stray bullets lodged in their roofs and on their premises. The residents near the cemetery say they are fearing for their lives. Carte Blanche investigates why this practice is being allowed and what police are doing to bring those responsible for shooting Margaret Holloway to book?

Summary:
Seventy six year old Margaret Holloway was standing in her home when she felt a burning sensation in her leg, she fell to the floor, cracked her head open and passed out. A while later she woke up in a pool of blood not knowing what had happened to her, she thought she had burst a vein in her leg as it was bleeding.

She crawled to get to her cell phone and call for help. When her friend took her to the hospital they speculated what it could be and then remembered the sound of the bullets from the funeral and thought maybe that’s what could have happened. After her Xrays were taken, it was confirmed that she had a bullet lodged in her leg, the surgeons are refusing to operate saying that it would be too dangerous for her, so now she has to live with the bullet lodged in her body.

“It is indeed a miraculous escape. My life was spared by two seconds. If I had not moved two steps forward, the bullet could have hit me on the back of my head. If it had not hit me on my leg, it would have killed me.”

Margaret says, “Normally there is a 21 gun salute but at these funerals it’s more like a 21 minute gun salute. She says the gunfire went on for about 30 minutes. Margaret wants justice and would like to know who is responsible for paying for her medical bills, as a pensioner living in an old age home, the cost has been too much for her.

Margaret Holloway is willing to give us an interview.

Another resident on the same day Hitesh Jeaven, heard a noise coming out of his 87 year old father’s bedroom, when he went in to see what had happened he saw glass shattered all over the floor and his father who suffers from a chronic heart condition had run out of the room from shear fright. On further inspection Hitesh Jeaven discovered a 9mm bullet which had smashed the window. He says, had it travelled 3 meters more it could have severely injured his father or killed him.

I am waiting for Hitesh Jeaven to let me know if he is willing to be interviewed.



Further information:
Clint Hill, a community activist was having a braai on the 31st of October, when he and his partner heard gunfire, he now knows to run inside and hide, as these incidents have been ongoing and over the last two months there has been gunfire from three funerals he says. Once they were inside taking cover they heard a loud noise coming from the roof. Later when the gunfire ceased he went to inspect the roof and found a 9mm bullet lodged there. He called the police, opened a case and handed them the bullet to investigate.

The funeral in process was that of ANC Regional Executive Committee member and former ANC Youth League Chairperson Desmond Mashele. He says the residents in the area are scared and outraged and that the police are too scared to tackle the issue because the people at these funerals are carrying weapons.

Clint Hill is willing to be interviewed.

Judy Ditchfield another resident, and wife of ex member of ‘The Bats’ Paul Ditchfield also heard the bullets this Saturday and they heard a loud noise on their roof, but because it’s two stories high they have been unable to go and see if they can find the bullet. She says that this firing at funerals is common place and that they are now afraid for their lives.

Judy Ditchfield is willing to be interviewed.

There are other case studies I could approach. I have been trying to contact Amy Scholtz who is a mother of two, and found a bullet in her yard, but have been unable to yet, she says she is worried about her children’s safety.

Can continue trying to get an interview with her.

James Lorimer MP - DA Constituency Head: Linden, Westdene and Montgomery Park was so outraged at the first incident where Margaret Holloway was injured that he raised it in Parliament where Bheki Cele said he would initiate an investigation. But since then there have been more firearms used at funrerals of ANC dignitaries.

James Lorimer is willing to be interviewed. He has been following the issue very closely.

The security company SCP filmed the incident from the outside and have given us permission to use their video. I was going to interview their CEO Clive Maher, but he has now declined the interview.

I think it would be great as part of the treatment to get a ballistics expert on board (as per John’s suggestion) who can speak of the bullet trajectories and the damage various bullets can cause. I am trying to get hold of Lobo Das Neves. As part of the treatment if I can fly a drone in the area, I would like to almost try and do a POV of the Bullet speeded up traveling from the cemetery to people’s houses. And to do a demonstration with the ballistics expert on how bullets travel.

I have requested an interview with SAPS Provincial spokesperson Brigadier Muridili, to find how far they are with the initial investigation and if they are close to making any arrests and if they have started their investigation regarding the incident of Oct 31st. And how is SAPS planning on dealing with these potentially deadly demonstrations at funerals.

We can also approach Brigadier Vish Naidoo, National Spokesperson rather, he did tell ENCA that the investigation was underway.

Deputy Secretary General, Jesse Duarte has asked for a probe after the first incident and condemned these displays. We can try and ask her for comment. I have not yet approached her.

The overall treatment will be telling personal narrative, with possible use of the drone if permitted in the area to illustrate distance from the cemetery to people’s homes as well as trying to do some bullet POV shots if we can pull it off. To use the ballistics expert in a way that illustrates the way the bullets travel and the harm they can cause, in a visually exciting way. Links and visuals to be filmed in the cemetery with a wry irony, playing on the resting place in contrast with violent and irrational acts that can cause severe harm.

Press Release:


In Westdene Johannesburg, residents are living in fear as live bullets allegedly from gun salute ceremonies at political funerals, are straying dangerously onto their properties - and one pensioner has already been seriously wounded


Script:


VO: On the 5th of September this year, in Westdene Johannesburg, 76-year-old Margaret Holloway was going about her day at her retirement village.

Margaret: I was feeding the birds on the pavement, I came around, I got to here, and I got this terrible pain in the back of my leg, so I sort of hobbled…
Mac: And all this time you don't know what's going on
Margaret: No, and I managed to get up here onto the chair. But as I got onto the chair, I passed out.
And I hit my head on, I landed on the floor there.

VO: As Holloway lay wounded, a few kilometres away, at West Park Cemetery, the funeral of ANC veteran Kebby Maphatsoe was underway.
In his honour, as president of Umkhonto We Sizwe Military Veterans Association, members of MKMVA, fired "supposed" blank rounds into the air.

VO: In the meantime, Holloway lay unconscious on her stoep, alone and helpless.

Margaret: And when I came around, it was just blood everywhere.

VO: She managed to crawl to her phone and call her friend Zoe, who came straight over. When they took off her bloodied pants they saw a small hole.

Margaret: So that's when I said to her, Zoe do you think I've been shot? Because we've been hearing the shooting all afternoon….

VO: She was rushed to the hospital.

Margaret: They didn't know what was going on either until they did the X rays. And then they saw that it was a bullet in my leg.

VO: A few weeks later on the 30th of October, just up the road from Holloway, Clint Hill and Kathleen Wolmarans were enjoying a peaceful afternoon.

Clint: We were busy with like a early afternoon braai and the next minute we heard the gunshots.

VO: What you're hearing is gunfire coming from the Westdene Montgomery Park area on the same day they heard the shots.

Link: They're being fired from right here inside Johannesburg's Westpark cemetery. And who's firing them? Mourners. A trend that has become more frequent at ANC VIP funerals.
UPSOUND: Bang bang bang

VO: Firearms expert, Lobo Das Neves studied video footage of the Kebby Maphatsoe funeral.

Lobo: Everything that they did there with firearms, everything is illegal. // You can't carry a firearm open in the public. Unless certain conditions are complied with which are absent here.

Mac: Tell us what's going on there. What firearms are being used?
Video plays
Lobo: So here you see a gentleman holding what appears to be a handgun, firing it rapidly into the air and there's a second person also holding a handgun after having fired into the air,
( Plays footage) there's no firearm safety, the firearms are being waved in all types of different directions
Mac: Could you assess whether this is live ammunition or not?
Lobo: One can see on the video that these firearms are cycling which means that a live round had to be fed into the firearm for it to actually function like a fully loaded and firing firearm.
VO: According to Das Neves these reckless displays can also endanger funeral-goers.
Lobo: So here you see this gentleman with an AK 47 firing at about a 45-degree angle into the air. Now two reasons you can see that this is live ammunition - there is no blank adapter in the front of the muzzle of the firearm. And secondly every time he fires it, the gun recoils. You see a second person also firing the same

VO: DA MP for Linden, James Lorimer, has serious concerns about reckless gun salutes at funerals, especially the one that may have caused Margaret Holloway's injury.

James: There was another elderly man in Montgomery Park who had a bullet come through the window of his bedroom and land just next to where he normally sits in his chair. It's only a matter of time before somebody is killed.
Mac: Police are around when these guns are being fired
James: It was something I brought up in Parliament. Police Minister Bheki Cele said the cases had been opened. But since then, it's been radio silence.

Lobo: The law's very clear that when a criminal offence is committed in the presence of a police officer, that police officer is obliged to act.

Link: I'm standing roundabout where Margaret was on that day. Now, when I look at my maps, it says West Park cemetery is about three and a half kilometres away. But as the crow flies, it's about a kilometre. That bullet must have travelled above all of these roofs through the trees and got lodged in Margaret's left leg. Now If she had maybe changed position slightly, it could have hit her in the back paralysing her, or even killing her!

Mac: This is from Margaret Holloway's X-ray…
Lobo: That there is clearly a rifle round. If you look at the dimensions, it looks like it could possibly be an AK 47 round.
Mac: How far can the bullets go
Lobo: it's not uncommon for a AK-47 round to travel up to a kilometre.
Mac: And still be lethal?
Lobo: And still be lethal.

Up sound Funeral: You can shoot.

VO: Carl Niehaus, spokesperson for the disbanded MKMVA was present at the funeral.

Carl Niehaus: It was an environment where comrades were sad, part of that expression of sadness, in the military context of the history of Umkhonto We Sizwe is that comrades shoot in the air.
Mac: Now we're at a point Carl, where somebody has been injured?
Carl Niehaus: It's not within my power to prove even that that bullet, which this elderly lady had been hit with came from a gun that was fired at the funeral. That is something which the South African police service has to do and once there is conclusive evidence then we can respond.

Carl: The call that we’ve made consistently was don't use live ammunition, use blanks. Please take into consideration the safety of the community.

Lobo: The problem is that to fire a blank round in the air, they have to display that firearm in public, and that's an offence.

VO: Das Neves took us to his shooting range for a live round versus blank demonstration.

Lobo: So these are, these are some of the different types of blanks that you get, so that's a handgun blank.
The purpose of this exercise is to prove scientifically that what we saw on the video were people firing live rounds and not blanks.
Show demo: of two gun fires
VO: First up - a 9mm parabellum with a live round. ///
The recoil is evident, as the spent cartridge is ejected and the next round cycles into place.
/// When firing the blank, there is no recoil or cycling.
Lobo: So these are different adapters that you would need on an AK 74 or an AK 47 to fire blanks. So an adapter like this would attach to the front of the barrel. And without this, the weapon wouldn't function normally like it would function with real live ammunition.
VO: Again with the rifle demonstration,
/// it’s clear that there is no recoil or cycling of ammunition when firing a blank.
Lobo: None of the weapons that I saw on the video footage had one of these on them. And the only assumption that one can make is that those were live rounds being fired from those weapons.

Clint: When they’re shooting over the koppies, it's obviously going to come down on our neighbourhood.

VO: It was on the day ANC Gauteng Executive Committee Member, Desmond Mashele was being buried, when Hill and Wolmeraans heard the gunshots and took cover inside.

Clint: And the next minute on the roof it was like a loud crack
Kat: I thought it was a branch that had fallen on the roof. It was such a loud bang.
Clint: There was like a spinning sound like a spinning top and I know from experience a bullet is turning, so the minute it landed and hit the roof, it was still turning
Kat: Then when Clint went up with a ladder, he actually, he confirmed that it actually was the bullet hitting the roof, I was quite amazed.

VO: Immediately they reported it to the police who came and collected the 9mm bullet

Kat: We spoke to them about our whole neighbourhood’s safety And they said to us that there wasn't a lot they could do about it, especially when people are so emotionally charged at a funeral and that they all just really stood by and watched these proceedings.

Link: Just in this area, three different households say they found bullets either on their roofs or on their property.

VO: We wanted answers from the ANC and the Police//
The ANC has not responded, even though Deputy Secretary-General Jessie Duarte asked for a probe into the Kebby Maphatsoe funeral.//
VO: The SAPS replied in writing and say they are investigating the shootings at the funerals, including the use of facial comparison tools, to identify those, who were filmed firing guns - no arrests have yet been made.

Lobo: A person that fires a round into the air and kills someone is guilty of murder because there is a reasonable foreseeability that a discharged round can kill another person.

VO: The SAPS say they are investigating allegations that police officers did not act immediately to arrest people firing randomly, and orders were issued to apply a multidisciplinary approach for the policing of high profile funerals.

James: Nothing is going to be done unless there is a lot of pressure on the police to actually take action.

VO: Investigations like these can be lengthy and in the meantime, Margaret Holloway's health is suffering - the doctors told her that removing the bullet was too dangerous.

Margaret: It's lodged against the bone, sitting somewhere here.
Mac: Do you feel any pain?
Margaret: The foot is a bit swollen so I don't know what to do.

Lobo: There's a big chance obviously of clotting and secondary damage from that bullet wound.

Mac: Are you comfortable with having to now live with this bullet lodged in your leg for the rest of your life?
Margaret: Not really but what can I do… I can't take it out myself.

November 2021 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 29 November 2021 Press Release: In Westdene Johannesburg, residents are living in fear as live bullets allegedly from gun salute ceremonies at political funerals, are straying dangerously onto their properties - and one pensioner has already been seriously wounded Script: VO: On the 5th of September this year, in Westdene Johannesburg, 76-year-old Margaret Holloway was going about her day at her retirement village. Margaret: I was feeding the birds on the pavement, I came around, I got to here, and I got this terrible pain in the back of my leg, so I sort of hobbled… Mac: And all this time you don't know what's going on Margaret: No, and I managed to get up here onto the chair. But as I got onto the chair, I passed out. And I hit my head on, I landed on the floor there. VO: As Holloway lay wounded, a few kilometres away, at West Park Cemetery, the funeral of ANC veteran Kebby Maphatsoe was underway. In his honour, as president of Umkhonto We Sizwe Military Veterans Association, members of MKMVA, fired "supposed" blank rounds into the air. VO: In the meantime, Holloway lay unconscious on her stoep, alone and helpless. Margaret: And when I came around, it was just blood everywhere. VO: She managed to crawl to her phone and call her friend Zoe, who came straight over. When they took off her bloodied pants they saw a small hole. Margaret: So that's when I said to her, Zoe do you think I've been shot? Because we've been hearing the shooting all afternoon…. VO: She was rushed to the hospital. Margaret: They didn't know what was going on either until they did the X rays. And then they saw that it was a bullet in my leg. VO: A few weeks later on the 30th of October, just up the road from Holloway, Clint Hill and Kathleen Wolmarans were enjoying a peaceful afternoon. Clint: We were busy with like a early afternoon braai and the next minute we heard the gunshots. VO: What you're hearing is gunfire coming from the Westdene Montgomery Park area on the same day they heard the shots. Link: They're being fired from right here inside Johannesburg's Westpark cemetery. And who's firing them? Mourners. A trend that has become more frequent at ANC VIP funerals. UPSOUND: Bang bang bang VO: Firearms expert, Lobo Das Neves studied video footage of the Kebby Maphatsoe funeral. Lobo: Everything that they did there with firearms, everything is illegal. // You can't carry a firearm open in the public. Unless certain conditions are complied with which are absent here. Mac: Tell us what's going on there. What firearms are being used? Video plays Lobo: So here you see a gentleman holding what appears to be a handgun, firing it rapidly into the air and there's a second person also holding a handgun after having fired into the air, ( Plays footage) there's no firearm safety, the firearms are being waved in all types of different directions Mac: Could you assess whether this is live ammunition or not? Lobo: One can see on the video that these firearms are cycling which means that a live round had to be fed into the firearm for it to actually function like a fully loaded and firing firearm. VO: According to Das Neves these reckless displays can also endanger funeral-goers. Lobo: So here you see this gentleman with an AK 47 firing at about a 45-degree angle into the air. Now two reasons you can see that this is live ammunition - there is no blank adapter in the front of the muzzle of the firearm. And secondly every time he fires it, the gun recoils. You see a second person also firing the same VO: DA MP for Linden, James Lorimer, has serious concerns about reckless gun salutes at funerals, especially the one that may have caused Margaret Holloway's injury. James: There was another elderly man in Montgomery Park who had a bullet come through the window of his bedroom and land just next to where he normally sits in his chair. It's only a matter of time before somebody is killed. Mac: Police are around when these guns are being fired James: It was something I brought up in Parliament. Police Minister Bheki Cele said the cases had been opened. But since then, it's been radio silence. Lobo: The law's very clear that when a criminal offence is committed in the presence of a police officer, that police officer is obliged to act. Link: I'm standing roundabout where Margaret was on that day. Now, when I look at my maps, it says West Park cemetery is about three and a half kilometres away. But as the crow flies, it's about a kilometre. That bullet must have travelled above all of these roofs through the trees and got lodged in Margaret's left leg. Now If she had maybe changed position slightly, it could have hit her in the back paralysing her, or even killing her! Mac: This is from Margaret Holloway's X-ray… Lobo: That there is clearly a rifle round. If you look at the dimensions, it looks like it could possibly be an AK 47 round. Mac: How far can the bullets go Lobo: it's not uncommon for a AK-47 round to travel up to a kilometre. Mac: And still be lethal? Lobo: And still be lethal. Up sound Funeral: You can shoot. VO: Carl Niehaus, spokesperson for the disbanded MKMVA was present at the funeral. Carl Niehaus: It was an environment where comrades were sad, part of that expression of sadness, in the military context of the history of Umkhonto We Sizwe is that comrades shoot in the air. Mac: Now we're at a point Carl, where somebody has been injured? Carl Niehaus: It's not within my power to prove even that that bullet, which this elderly lady had been hit with came from a gun that was fired at the funeral. That is something which the South African police service has to do and once there is conclusive evidence then we can respond. Carl: The call that we’ve made consistently was don't use live ammunition, use blanks. Please take into consideration the safety of the community. Lobo: The problem is that to fire a blank round in the air, they have to display that firearm in public, and that's an offence. VO: Das Neves took us to his shooting range for a live round versus blank demonstration. Lobo: So these are, these are some of the different types of blanks that you get, so that's a handgun blank. The purpose of this exercise is to prove scientifically that what we saw on the video were people firing live rounds and not blanks. Show demo: of two gun fires VO: First up - a 9mm parabellum with a live round. /// The recoil is evident, as the spent cartridge is ejected and the next round cycles into place. /// When firing the blank, there is no recoil or cycling. Lobo: So these are different adapters that you would need on an AK 74 or an AK 47 to fire blanks. So an adapter like this would attach to the front of the barrel. And without this, the weapon wouldn't function normally like it would function with real live ammunition. VO: Again with the rifle demonstration, /// it’s clear that there is no recoil or cycling of ammunition when firing a blank. Lobo: None of the weapons that I saw on the video footage had one of these on them. And the only assumption that one can make is that those were live rounds being fired from those weapons. Clint: When they’re shooting over the koppies, it's obviously going to come down on our neighbourhood. VO: It was on the day ANC Gauteng Executive Committee Member, Desmond Mashele was being buried, when Hill and Wolmeraans heard the gunshots and took cover inside. Clint: And the next minute on the roof it was like a loud crack Kat: I thought it was a branch that had fallen on the roof. It was such a loud bang. Clint: There was like a spinning sound like a spinning top and I know from experience a bullet is turning, so the minute it landed and hit the roof, it was still turning Kat: Then when Clint went up with a ladder, he actually, he confirmed that it actually was the bullet hitting the roof, I was quite amazed. VO: Immediately they reported it to the police who came and collected the 9mm bullet Kat: We spoke to them about our whole neighbourhood’s safety And they said to us that there wasn't a lot they could do about it, especially when people are so emotionally charged at a funeral and that they all just really stood by and watched these proceedings. Link: Just in this area, three different households say they found bullets either on their roofs or on their property. VO: We wanted answers from the ANC and the Police// The ANC has not responded, even though Deputy Secretary-General Jessie Duarte asked for a probe into the Kebby Maphatsoe funeral.// VO: The SAPS replied in writing and say they are investigating the shootings at the funerals, including the use of facial comparison tools, to identify those, who were filmed firing guns - no arrests have yet been made. Lobo: A person that fires a round into the air and kills someone is guilty of murder because there is a reasonable foreseeability that a discharged round can kill another person. VO: The SAPS say they are investigating allegations that police officers did not act immediately to arrest people firing randomly, and orders were issued to apply a multidisciplinary approach for the policing of high profile funerals. James: Nothing is going to be done unless there is a lot of pressure on the police to actually take action. VO: Investigations like these can be lengthy and in the meantime, Margaret Holloway's health is suffering - the doctors told her that removing the bullet was too dangerous. Margaret: It's lodged against the bone, sitting somewhere here. Mac: Do you feel any pain? Margaret: The foot is a bit swollen so I don't know what to do. Lobo: There's a big chance obviously of clotting and secondary damage from that bullet wound. Mac: Are you comfortable with having to now live with this bullet lodged in your leg for the rest of your life? Margaret: Not really but what can I do… I can't take it out myself.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It’s an emotional quagmire around Johannesburg’s Westpark Cemetery - gun salutes as the deceased are being laid to rest are disturbing the peace and endangering the lives of local residents.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Rest in peace is what we hope for when people we care about go to their final resting place. But there is no rest for the living, when ANC VIP funerals are commemorated with sprays of unrelenting gunfire, threatening the lives of innocent people who live in near the cemeteries. When 76 year old Margaret Holloway was hit in the leg by a stray bullet in her home in Westdene, from disbanded MKMVA Kebby Maphatsoe’s funeral at Westpark Cemetery in September this year, it made headlines. National Police spokesperson Vish Naidoo, said that an investigation had been launched and people would be held accountable. When asked why the police who were present at the funeral did not act immediately, he likened the situation on ENCA to Marikana, stating that the police were preventing further bloodshed as many people were armed. ANC Deptuty Secretary Jesse Duarte called on law enforcement for a probe on what happened and condemned the firing of guns at funerals. A month later there have been no arrests. Just this weekend at the funeral of ANC Regional Executive Committee member and former ANC Youth League Chairperson Desmond Mashele another round of bullets were fired, this time no one was injured, but many residents around Westdene and Montgomery Park, ran for cover when they heard the gunshots which lasted for over 20 minutes. They found stray bullets lodged in their roofs and on their premises. The residents near the cemetery say they are fearing for their lives. Carte Blanche investigates why this practice is being allowed and what police are doing to bring those responsible for shooting Margaret Holloway to book?
metadata.Summary: Seventy six year old Margaret Holloway was standing in her home when she felt a burning sensation in her leg, she fell to the floor, cracked her head open and passed out. A while later she woke up in a pool of blood not knowing what had happened to her, she thought she had burst a vein in her leg as it was bleeding. She crawled to get to her cell phone and call for help. When her friend took her to the hospital they speculated what it could be and then remembered the sound of the bullets from the funeral and thought maybe that’s what could have happened. After her Xrays were taken, it was confirmed that she had a bullet lodged in her leg, the surgeons are refusing to operate saying that it would be too dangerous for her, so now she has to live with the bullet lodged in her body. “It is indeed a miraculous escape. My life was spared by two seconds. If I had not moved two steps forward, the bullet could have hit me on the back of my head. If it had not hit me on my leg, it would have killed me.” Margaret says, “Normally there is a 21 gun salute but at these funerals it’s more like a 21 minute gun salute. She says the gunfire went on for about 30 minutes. Margaret wants justice and would like to know who is responsible for paying for her medical bills, as a pensioner living in an old age home, the cost has been too much for her. Margaret Holloway is willing to give us an interview. Another resident on the same day Hitesh Jeaven, heard a noise coming out of his 87 year old father’s bedroom, when he went in to see what had happened he saw glass shattered all over the floor and his father who suffers from a chronic heart condition had run out of the room from shear fright. On further inspection Hitesh Jeaven discovered a 9mm bullet which had smashed the window. He says, had it travelled 3 meters more it could have severely injured his father or killed him. I am waiting for Hitesh Jeaven to let me know if he is willing to be interviewed.
metadata.Further information: Clint Hill, a community activist was having a braai on the 31st of October, when he and his partner heard gunfire, he now knows to run inside and hide, as these incidents have been ongoing and over the last two months there has been gunfire from three funerals he says. Once they were inside taking cover they heard a loud noise coming from the roof. Later when the gunfire ceased he went to inspect the roof and found a 9mm bullet lodged there. He called the police, opened a case and handed them the bullet to investigate. The funeral in process was that of ANC Regional Executive Committee member and former ANC Youth League Chairperson Desmond Mashele. He says the residents in the area are scared and outraged and that the police are too scared to tackle the issue because the people at these funerals are carrying weapons. Clint Hill is willing to be interviewed. Judy Ditchfield another resident, and wife of ex member of ‘The Bats’ Paul Ditchfield also heard the bullets this Saturday and they heard a loud noise on their roof, but because it’s two stories high they have been unable to go and see if they can find the bullet. She says that this firing at funerals is common place and that they are now afraid for their lives. Judy Ditchfield is willing to be interviewed. There are other case studies I could approach. I have been trying to contact Amy Scholtz who is a mother of two, and found a bullet in her yard, but have been unable to yet, she says she is worried about her children’s safety. Can continue trying to get an interview with her. James Lorimer MP - DA Constituency Head: Linden, Westdene and Montgomery Park was so outraged at the first incident where Margaret Holloway was injured that he raised it in Parliament where Bheki Cele said he would initiate an investigation. But since then there have been more firearms used at funrerals of ANC dignitaries. James Lorimer is willing to be interviewed. He has been following the issue very closely. The security company SCP filmed the incident from the outside and have given us permission to use their video. I was going to interview their CEO Clive Maher, but he has now declined the interview. I think it would be great as part of the treatment to get a ballistics expert on board (as per John’s suggestion) who can speak of the bullet trajectories and the damage various bullets can cause. I am trying to get hold of Lobo Das Neves. As part of the treatment if I can fly a drone in the area, I would like to almost try and do a POV of the Bullet speeded up traveling from the cemetery to people’s houses. And to do a demonstration with the ballistics expert on how bullets travel. I have requested an interview with SAPS Provincial spokesperson Brigadier Muridili, to find how far they are with the initial investigation and if they are close to making any arrests and if they have started their investigation regarding the incident of Oct 31st. And how is SAPS planning on dealing with these potentially deadly demonstrations at funerals. We can also approach Brigadier Vish Naidoo, National Spokesperson rather, he did tell ENCA that the investigation was underway. Deputy Secretary General, Jesse Duarte has asked for a probe after the first incident and condemned these displays. We can try and ask her for comment. I have not yet approached her. The overall treatment will be telling personal narrative, with possible use of the drone if permitted in the area to illustrate distance from the cemetery to people’s homes as well as trying to do some bullet POV shots if we can pull it off. To use the ballistics expert in a way that illustrates the way the bullets travel and the harm they can cause, in a visually exciting way. Links and visuals to be filmed in the cemetery with a wry irony, playing on the resting place in contrast with violent and irrational acts that can cause severe harm.
